name: Noise Level Estimation
description: Estimates local noise levels using PCA-based methods — regions with inconsistent noise levels indicate compositing or AI generation.
mechanism:
This method estimates image noise levels using Principal Component Analysis to separate noise from image content, enabling detection of regions with inconsistent noise properties:

1. **Patch-Based PCA Decomposition**: The image is divided into overlapping patches of size P×P (typically 7×7 or 9×9). Each patch is vectorized into a P²-dimensional vector. A set of M patches (typically M > 10×P²) from homogeneous regions is selected using a gradient-based pre-filter. PCA is applied to the patch covariance matrix Σ = (1/M) Σᵢ xᵢxᵢᵀ, yielding eigenvalues λ₁ ≥ λ₂ ≥ ... ≥ λ_{P²}. The noise variance is estimated from the smallest eigenvalues, which capture noise rather than signal structure.

2. **Eigenvalue-Based Noise Estimation**: Following Liu et al. (2013), the noise variance σ² is estimated by finding the threshold k* that separates signal eigenvalues from noise eigenvalues. For additive white Gaussian noise, the noise eigenvalues cluster near σ²: σ² = (1/(P²−k*)) Σᵢ₌ₖ*₊₁ᴾ² λᵢ. The optimal k* is determined by minimizing the median absolute deviation of eigenvalues above the threshold, ensuring robust separation of signal and noise subspaces.

3. **Local Noise Level Mapping**: The PCA-based estimation is applied to overlapping spatial windows (64×64 to 128×128 pixels) across the image, producing a spatially varying noise level map σ(x,y). For authentic photographs, this map should follow the signal-dependent Poisson-Gaussian noise model: σ²(I) = a·I + b, where I is the local intensity, a is the gain parameter (shot noise), and b is the read noise variance. Deviations from this model indicate regions with different noise origins.

4. **Forensic Analysis via Noise Clustering**: The local noise estimates are clustered using k-means (k=2,3) to identify regions with distinct noise profiles. In composited images, spliced regions form a separate cluster with different (a,b) parameters. AI-generated regions typically show anomalously low noise levels or noise without the characteristic signal-dependent structure. The method reports the cluster assignments and inter-cluster noise level difference as forgery indicators.
parameters:
Patch size: 7×7 or 9×9 pixels
PCA sample count: > 500 patches per window
Spatial window: 64×64 or 128×128 pixels
Window overlap: 50%
Noise model: Poisson-Gaussian σ²(I) = aI + b
Clustering: k-means with k = 2 or 3
Minimum image size: 256×256 pixels
accuracy: 84–92% noise estimation accuracy (within ±1.5 of ground truth σ). Noise inconsistency-based splicing detection achieves F1-score of 0.86. AI-generated image detection: 81–87% for images with unnaturally smooth or absent noise. Poisson-Gaussian model fitting achieves R² > 0.95 on authentic photographs.
source: Liu, C., Szeliski, R., Kang, S. B., Zitnick, C. L. & Freeman, W. T. (2008). Automatic Estimation and Removal of Noise from a Single Image. IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence, 30(2), 299–314.
useCase: Estimating camera sensor noise characteristics for source identification. Detecting composited regions with mismatched noise profiles. Identifying AI-generated images lacking natural camera noise. Calibrating denoising algorithms with accurate noise level estimates.
strengths:
• PCA-based estimation separates noise from signal without denoising
• Signal-dependent noise model provides physically grounded analysis
• Local estimation enables spatial anomaly detection
• Works on single images without reference or camera calibration
• Robust to diverse image content (textures, edges, smooth regions)
limitations:
• Requires sufficient homogeneous patches for reliable PCA estimation
• JPEG compression introduces quantization noise that complicates estimation
• Resized or interpolated images alter the noise structure
• Some AI generators add realistic synthetic noise to evade detection
• Very low noise images (high-ISO denoised or studio lighting) provide less discriminative power
